item.title: Trump-backed crypto bill fails to launch as Dems, Republicans unite to block it
item.description: Sen. Cynthia Lummis declared the Clarity Act dead after Democrats and some Republicans blocked the massive crypto regulation bill in a key Senate vote.
item.content:encoded:
A colossal crypto regulatory package backed by President Donald Trump stumbled in the Senate, and another shot is unlikely.

The Clarity Act failed to move through a key procedural hurdle on Tuesday, serving proponents of the bill, including major players in the cryptocurrency industry and the White House, a major blow in their pursuit of folding the novel currency into the nation’s web of financial regulations.

Democrats dealt the bill a mortal blow, but a handful of Republicans with outstanding concerns were not assuaged, either. And with little time left on the Senate’s calendar and major bills piling up ahead of the midterm elections, the bill’s biggest backers believed that the Clarity Act might end up back on the shelf.

REPUBLICANS TARGET TRUMP'S CRYPTO EMPIRE WITH NEW PLAN, DEMS SAY IT FALLS SHORT

"I think we're done. It's over," Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., the bill’s primary architect, said. "Because we've been working on this bill for over a year. And we've given them over 120 of their requests and that’s enough."

When asked if the bill would come back to the floor, Lummis said, "Nope."

A midnight hour update was made to the bill to try and pull anyone on the fence off to at least let the package move forward. But it wasn’t enough.

DEMOCRATS HAND TRUMP ONE POWER THEY SPENT YEARS FIGHTING

"I haven't seen the final bill yet, but what I've seen is bad," Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., told Fox News Digital before the vote.

The issues with the package were many and varying among Democrats and Republicans. Several Senate Democrats were not satisfied with the ethics language baked into the Clarity Act that sought to slow Trump’s family’s rapidly growing crypto empire.

That’s because Trump’s income between 2024 and 2025 erupted by about 250% — from just over $620 million to about $2.2 billion.

And much of that increase is attributed to his various holdings and ventures in crypto, which are run by his sons, Don Jr. and Eric, according to the president’s financial disclosure forms reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Others didn’t believe that the language dealing with foreign money laundering had enough teeth.

"I have not seen the kind of engagement yet from the Republican side when it comes to countering terrorist financing and cartel financing. That would get me to a yes," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said. "I'm still engaged. I didn't get on board with the GENIUS Act till the very last vote."

TRUMP'S $5,000 DIVIDEND CHECKS WOULD COME WITH A MAJOR CATCH UNDER GOP SENATOR'S PLAN

Still, some lawmakers argued they should at least move forward with the bill to tweak it as needed.

Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, was still undecided before the vote. He was worried about how bringing crypto into the fold could affect deposit yields at community banks and guardrails on the currency being "diverted for criminal purposes," but he argued the bill could be strengthened if they moved forward.

"What we used to do around here is something called legislate," Cornyn said. "You know where you'd actually vote to get on the bill, but then you amend it, and then you decide whether you're going to support it on the back end."

The bill’s failure does open up the Senate to speedily move to other legislative priorities, like Sen. Ted Cruz's, R-Texas, college sports bill to add protections to student-athletes and slow the big money train ripping through collegiate athletics.

"We committed to ensure that we got a vote on college sports," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said. "So we'll see if we have 60 [votes]. I don't know the answer for sure to that yet. I hope we do."

item.title: Liberal lawmakers, activists rally behind Macklemore after Sheeran tour removal over 'Free Palestine' stance
item.description: Macklemore claims Robert Kraft rallied stadium owners to force Ed Sheeran's hand, sparking a free speech debate over his pro-Palestinian stance.
item.content:encoded:
Liberal lawmakers, commentators and activists have spoken out against Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's tour and expressed support for the rapper.

"It’s so incredibly disappointing that Macklemore, my constituent, was removed from Ed Sheeran’s tour because of his comments in support of the Palestinian people. We should all be outraged that powerful people are more upset about what an artist says than the displacement, starvation, and killing of innocent Palestinian children and families. Thank you, Macklemore, for speaking up. This is a moment for us to come together, find our moral conscience as a nation, and end this genocide," Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., wrote on X.

After Macklemore repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Ed Sheeran, the rapper was dropped Monday from the remaining U.S. dates on which he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's "Loop Tour."

MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."

Kraft provided a statement to TMZ, confirming that he opposed Macklemore performing at Gillette Stadium: "Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech."

He added, "Based on Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line." 

However, Kraft concluded, "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf."

Children's YouTuber Ms. Rachel criticized Sheeran specifically in her comments on Instagram.

PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS

Macklemore's announcement about the removal said Ed Sheeran and his team "removed" him from the tour.

He said he was dropped after New England Patriots owner and Gillette Stadium operator Robert Kraft had told Sheeran that the rapper would not be allowed to perform at the stadium.

ED SHEERAN CONCERT WORKERS HOSPITALIZED AFTER FORKLIFT INCIDENT IN DETROIT: REPORT

"Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium," Macklemore wrote. "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

"Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won't be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine," her post read. "Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it."

Macklemore was slated to appear at eight of the 10 shows left on the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour.

Rosie O'Donnell, a former co-host of "The View" who moved to Ireland after President Donald Trump was elected in 2024, also posted in support of Macklemore on Instagram.

"Wow — sad — I stand with him in solidarity #GENOCIDE," O'Donnell wrote in an Instagram post about the news. The actress screenshotted her comment and posted it to her own profile as well.

O'Donnell also posted several Instagram stories in support of Macklemore, with some referencing a boycott.

Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., expressed support for Macklemore on X, writing, "Admire your courage, Macklemore!"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

MUNA, a pop band, posted to its Instagram story writing, "Everyone involved in the move to silence free speech about a genocide is utterly pathetic. Solidarity with @macklemore."

"Hollywood in Toto Podcast" host Christian Toto said the lawmakers supporting Macklemore were suspiciously silent during other recent celebrity controversies.

"These same lawmakers were silent when Gina Carano was cancelled and her career was destroyed by Disney for an innocuous post about tolerance," Toto told Fox News Digital in a statement. "They also said nothing when British singer M.I.A. got booted from Kid Cudi's tour earlier this year for sharing right-leaning views."

"Don't they care about strong, empowered women being silenced?" he continued. "Here, the free speech argument is trickier. An opening musical act shouldn't dramatically differ from the headliner. If Ed Sheeran's brand is family friendly and apolitical, having someone like Macklemore start his shows makes little sense. The situation could have been resolved by the musicians setting up boundaries for their opening act's political statements. Macklemore is an employee of the tour and represents Sheeran's brand, to a degree."

Sheeran's team did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News Digital also reached out to a Kraft representative for comment.

item.title: Kennedy Center board votes to immediately close main building over safety, financial concerns
item.description: Fox News Digital confirmed Tuesday the Kennedy Center board voted to immediately close the building, citing safety and funding concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Fox News Digital confirmed Tuesday that the Kennedy Center board voted to immediately close the main building of the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., citing safety and funding concerns.

Two additional sources told Fox News the board approved the closure during a special meeting. A public statement is expected.

The vote came hours after a federal judge again blocked the Kennedy Center from adding President Donald Trump’s name to the building and plaza.

EXCLUSIVE: KENNEDY CENTER BOARD MOVES TO NAME GROUNDS ‘PRESIDENT DONALD J TRUMP PLAZA'

Judge Christopher Cooper ruled the Center cannot install the proposed Trump memorials without congressional approval.

It was not immediately clear how long the Kennedy Center will remain closed or how Tuesday’s court ruling could affect the closure.

This is a developing story; check back later for updates.

Fox News' Bill Mears contributed to this reporting.

I always have a lot of ideas on how to make sports better. I've always said that sports betting is a great way to make games more interesting, and it should be legal everywhere. Clearly, people seem to share that view, since it's become more accessible across America. One other thing I think baseball should do is eliminate the division system. I've also said that if you have a losing team for 10+ years, you should be forced to sell it. There are three that have a line of -225 or longer, and we are going to pick one to bet on that might give us a juicy payday.

This game features one of the worst teams in baseball against the best team in the American League. The Athletics are currently 28 games under .500, and seem like most of the players of substance on their team have been shut down for the year. Nick Kurtz is out, Shea Langeliers was hurt and is now just playing DH. Their pitching staff has been hurt as well, with J.T. Ginn, Luis Severino, and Gage Jump all injured. The Rays are gearing up for the postseason and are still one of the better teams in baseball. They also have the American League East to play for as they haven't quite kept the Yankees from having a shot at the division.

WITH ONE MONTH LEFT, AMERICAN LEAGUE TEAMS ARE HEADING TOWARDS AN EMBARRASSING, HISTORIC LOW

The Rays are currently a -239 favorite for tonight's game against the Athletics. Jack Perkins, the A's starter, has a 6.53 ERA for the year. Griffin Jax, who goes for the Rays, has a 3.99 ERA. I don't think this is the right game to play in terms of taking a shot on the A's. I just don't see it happening.

History classes used to talk about the "haves" and the "have-nots." That's kind of how you should view this game. The Los Angeles Dodgers have everything you would want out of a team. They are 91-59 for the season and still have an outside shot at winning 100 games. They may not look quite as dominant given the struggles of some players on their offense, but this team isn't worried about the regular season; they want the World Series. The Reds are 70-80 and a bit disappointing after making the postseason last year.

The Brewers are the best team in baseball and continue to try to secure home-field advantage throughout the postseason. Milwaukee has the pieces and has put together a great campaign. However, if we think the Dodgers are built for the postseason, the Brewers are definitely built for the regular season. The Pirates are .500, which is a step in the right direction, but they need to continue to advance forward in the offseason if they want to make a real threat at the playoffs next year.

Jacob Misiorowski, the NL Cy Young winner (soon enough), will take the mound tonight. However, one team he didn't look great against this season is the Pirates. He allowed three earned runs on six hits in his lone start against Pittsburgh. He also has a worse ERA on the road than at home this season. Lake Bachar, pitching for the Pirates, has a 3.52 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP. He has been strong in his four home starts with a 2.02 ERA. item.title: GOP Rep Thomas Massie introduces 8 articles of impeachment against War Secretary Pete Hegseth
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie read eight articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth on the House floor, citing War Powers Resolution violations in Iran.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduced a resolution to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and read eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth on the House floor Tuesday.

Massie formally entered a resolution to impeach Hegseth for "high crimes and misdemeanors" on the House floor for, among other things, allegedly violating the War Powers Resolution of 1973 in Iran and for his role in the operation that led to former Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro's capture and extradition.

The first three of the eight articles of impeachment Massie introduced accused Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution of 1973, arguing that Hegseth's Department of War is "waging the Iran war despite no declaration of war, statutory authorization, attack on the United States, or imminent threat."

His first article seeks to establish "that the war was unlawful from its inception." The second article claims that Hegseth disobeyed Congress after both the House and the Senate directed the removal of troops from Iran. The third article claims that Hegseth is "continuing hostilities in Iran after expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period."

4 HOUSE REPUBLICANS REBEL AGAINST TRUMP, VOTE WITH DEMS TO BLOCK IRAN WAR POWERS

The fourth and fifth articles accuse Hegseth of refusing to minimize civilian casualties and engaging in extrajudicial killing, with the latter charge accusing Hegseth of "replacing maritime law enforcement with unauthorized lethal military targeting of suspected drug traffickers" during operations striking suspected narcotraffickers in the Caribbean Sea.

REP SETH MOULTON SAYS HEGSETH IS 'GUILTY' OF WAR CRIMES, LINKS HIM TO NAZIS TRIED DURING WORLD WAR II

Also related to military action in the Caribbean and South America, Massie's seventh article accuses Hegseth of the "Kidnapping of a Sovereign Foreign Leader" for his role in Operation Absolute Resolve, the January mission in which U.S. Special Forces apprehended and extracted former Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores from Caracas. Massie's article condemns Hegseth for doing so "without constitutional or legal authority."

Article six accuses Hegseth of using his authority to suppress the free speech of Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., by retaliating against the senator for his video in which the senator joined a group of other lawmakers in a video which critics claimed encourage active military members to disobey lawful orders.

The final article charges Hegseth with carrying out unlawful orders in Yemen. The article "charges Secretary Hegseth with initiating Operation Rough Rider without congressional authorization or an imminent threat to the United States, while also violating war powers reporting requirements. It further addresses extensive civilian deaths and unlawful strikes on civilian objects, rescuers, and other protected persons."

After reading out his articles for over an hour on the House floor, Massie closed out his introduction.

"In all of this, Secretary Hegseth abused the powers entrusted to him as Secretary of Defense by subordinating the constitutional limits on the use of military force and the laws governing the conduct of hostilities to his own policy objectives," Massie said.

Massie also added that Hegseth "has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to civilians, the lawful conduct of United States military operations, the integrity and credibility of the United States Armed Forces and the Constitution, if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties, and the rule of law.

This, Massie said, "warrants impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States."

Fox News Digital contacted Massie's office and the Pentagon for further comment.

item.title: Cleveland Guardians look to even divisional series as Chicago White Sox cling to AL Central lead
item.description: The Chicago White Sox still lead the AL Central, but Foster Griffin and the Cleveland Guardians look poised to close the gap in this key series.
item.content:encoded:
Over the years, baseball has been one of the best sports for me to bet on. It isn't always the most glamorous, because most people don't watch every or any baseball games. Football is still king when it comes to watching and watch parties, but there are some great opportunities to make money betting on baseball. I think I've found one of those opportunities here as the White Sox take on the Guardians.

The Chicago White Sox still lead the American League Central. I can't believe that I just wrote that sentence in the middle of September. This has been a fun team to watch after the disastrous few seasons. They are a young team that probably doesn't even realize they shouldn't be in these situations yet. However, it is great experience, and if they do make it to the postseason, they may even get a bye in the first round given how the setup is for the postseason.

They still need to get past the Guardians, though. In an effort to take the series for the White Sox, Davis Martin is taking the ball. Martin was great in the early portion of the season, but hasn't pitched very well over the past few months. Through May, his ERA was 2.00. Through June, it was at 3.00, which was still very respectable. At the end of July, he was at 3.62, and August ended at 4.32. He has been solid in September, going 10.2 innings, allowing just nine hits, one earned run, and four strikeouts. He has faced Cleveland twice and allowed three earned runs over 4.1 innings of work against them.

The Cleveland Guardians are reminding me a lot of last season. If you recall, this team was basically asleep until August. Then, coupled with an all-time collapse from the Tigers, they turned it on and racked up the wins. They stole the AL Central last year. This season, the White Sox never had the distance between them that Detroit had last year. However, the Guardians never could find a way to stay consistently ahead of the White Sox.

Tonight their goal is to get the game they lost last night back from their divisional foes. They do it with an arm they added at the trade deadline, Foster Griffin. 

This has been a strong year for Griffin. He has gone 15-5 this season with a 3.65 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP. It hasn't been all rainbows and sunshine since he came to the Guardians. He has allowed 22 earned runs in 33.1 innings of work. However, 13 of those runs came in 6.1 innings of work. He dominated the White Sox this year when he was with the Nationals, going seven innings, allowing two hits and no earned runs.

This is the last series between the two clubs, and the White Sox are ahead of the Guardians 7-4 so far this year. However, tonight should make that a bit closer for the Guardians. Griffin on the mound gives them a great opportunity to win the game. Martin has been good for the White Sox, and he has pitched better lately, but it seems like the Guardians know what they are doing against him. Give me the Guardians on the run line at +144 today.

item.title: Kash Patel reveals FBI's capture of all 10 members of Most Wanted fugitive's list during hearing
item.description: Kash Patel told the Senate Judiciary Committee the FBI captured a fugitive in Venezuela tied to Tren de Aragua, completing a historic clean sweep.
item.content:encoded:
The FBI has apprehended all 10 members of the FBI's Most Wanted list during President Donald Trump's second term, FBI Director Kash Patel revealed during an appearance in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday.

Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, during his opening statements as the committee's chairman, lauded Patel and the FBI for their work in capturing nine of the 10 most wanted fugitives on the FBI's top 10 list.

Patel, during his opening remarks, corrected Grassley, revealing that his agency had just this past weekend caught the tenth fugitive.

"Mr. Chairman, I'm proud to announce today, and I hate to correct you, we haven't captured nine of the top 10 most [wanted] individuals on our list. We've captured 10," Patel said.

FBI CAPTURES TOP TEN MOST WANTED FUGITIVE WITH ALLEGED SINALOA CARTEL TIES, PATEL SAYS

"Just this past weekend, we captured a thug down in Venezuela who was on our most wanted list and on the run for years. He has been captured, apprehended and is on his way back to the United States of America. That's 10 of 10. Nobody in the FBI history has done that," Patel said.

HIGHEST-RANKING TREN DE ARAGUA MEMBER EVER EXTRADITED TO US SET TO APPEAR IN HOUSTON COURTROOM: DOJ

"We, the FBI, captured more than two and a half times the number of the top 10 most wanted fugitives on the FBI's list from the prior administration," he also said.

While Patel did not say the name of the fugitive during the hearing, the FBI earlier revealed exclusively to Fox News Digital that the 10th capture was that of Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, the FBI's first ever "cyber fugitive."

Aguirre led "a large international conspiracy to steal millions of dollars from financial institutions in support of the Tren de Aragua, through an ATM jackpotting scheme since at least 2024," the FBI told Fox News Digital.

In addition to a clean sweep of the top 10 fugitives, Patel also revealed that his FBI has also captured six of the top 10 most wanted fraudsters on the top 10 fraudsters list, a compilation his FBI created during the current administration.

FBI TOUTS 6,000 ARRESTS, 44% HOMICIDE DROP ONE YEAR INTO TRUMP'S DC CRIME CRACKDOWN

Patel also outlined the broader progress the Trump administration has made towards making the U.S. safer.

"On top of that, we've captured six of the most wanted fraudsters around the world, taking the murder rate down 20 points is no easy effort. It requires a team lift, state, local and international partners. This includes results in cities like Baltimore, which reached its lowest mid-year homicide numbers in recorded history," he said.

TRUMP’S LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS, GUNS IN BLUE CITY

"This year in Memphis, we accomplished a 50% reduction in homicide for a city that had the highest per capita homicide rate in the country, thanks to the president's task force. And right here in Washington, D.C., we are on track to have the lowest homicide numbers since 1990," Patel added.

Fox News Digital contacted the FBI for further comment.

Fox News Digital's Bonny Chu contributed to this report.

item.title: Colbert wins Emmy after show's cancellation but avoids discussing Trump
item.description: Stephen Colbert dodged questions about Trump's role in canceling "The Late Show" after winning an Emmy, while the White House fired back sharply.
item.content:encoded:
The White House on Tuesday denied President Donald Trump had any role in CBS' decision to cancel "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert," after the former late-night host dodged a question about Trump following his Emmy win in Los Angeles and defended the state of free speech.

Colbert's former program won Outstanding Variety Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards Monday, months after "The Late Show" aired its final episode in May. 

When asked after the ceremony about free speech and the future of late-night television, Colbert said he remained optimistic about the medium.

"If you can’t say something because you go to jail, that is a violation of free speech," Colbert said. "I think that late night is just as funny and just as vital as it ever has been, and I love watching Jimmy and Jimmy and John and John and Seth and everybody else. And I think I hope it goes on for a long time because you get to work with people like this, and that’s the greatest gift."

STEPHEN COLBERT EMERGES FROM CANCELLATION TO URGE EMMY VOTERS TO SELECT JIMMY KIMMEL OVER OWN SHOW

White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital the administration had nothing to do with the network’s decision.

"Neither President Trump nor anyone else in the Administration had anything to do with this," Ingle said, in a Tuesday statement to Fox News Digital. "The reality is Stephen Colbert is a pathetic trainwreck with no talent, which is exactly why CBS canceled his show and is booting him off the airwaves."

When CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister asked Colbert directly whether he believed his show had been canceled because of Trump, the comedian appeared to repeatedly deflect rather than answer the question. 

Variety reported that the exchange came during a post-Emmys interview with Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh.

COLBERT LASHES OUT AT CBS, SAYS CANCELLATION ‘REINFORCED A NARRATIVE’ OF ‘KNEE BENDING’ TO TRUMP

"What... Gayle, that’s a beautiful dress," Colbert said. After the reporter repeated the question, Colbert continued the bit. "Oh, I’m sorry, I’m deaf on this ear. What did you... what did you say?" Colbert said.

When they again attempted to ask whether Trump was responsible for the cancellation, Colbert deflected once more. "You wanted to know who the most important member of my staff was? It’s me," Colbert said.

Media Research Center President David Bozell told Fox News Digital on Tuesday that Colbert’s refusal to address the Trump question stood in contrast to the speculation surrounding the cancellation and pointed to CBS’ financial rationale for ending the show.

"Colbert suddenly does not want to talk about Trump? That’s rich. Obviously, Trump did not cancel his show," he said. "CBS looked at the audience, looked at the bill, and decided the joke had run long enough."

JIMMY KIMMEL SAYS HE FELT 'DEFEATED' AFTER COLBERT SHOW WAS CANCELLED, SAYS CBS IS USING 'MADE-UP NUMBERS'

CBS announced in July 2025 that it would end "The Late Show" franchise after Colbert's 25-26 season, calling the move "purely a financial decision against a challenging backdrop in late night." The network said the decision was unrelated to the show's performance, content or other matters involving then-parent company Paramount.

The announcement came three days after Colbert attacked Paramount over its $16 million settlement with Trump involving a "60 Minutes" interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris. Colbert characterized the agreement as a payoff connected to Paramount’s pending merger with Skydance Media.

"I believe this kind of complicated financial sentiment with a sitting government official has a technical name in legal circles. It’s ‘big fat bribe,’ because it all comes as Paramount’s owners are trying to get the Trump administration to approve the sale of our network to a new owner, Skydance!" Colbert said at the time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Fox News Digital reported that Colbert's manager, James Dixon, had been informed June 27 that CBS intended to end the show, before Paramount announced the Trump settlement and more than two weeks before Colbert publicly attacked the agreement. "The Late Show" had been losing roughly $40 million annually.

The FCC approved Paramount's $8 billion merger with Skydance one week after CBS announced the cancellation. The transaction later closed in August 2025.

Trump continued criticizing Colbert after the program’s May finale, calling the former CBS host talentless and celebrating his departure from late-night television.

Fox News Digital reached out to CBS-Paramount for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Man with an unbelievably swollen face arrested after Wichita golf course brawl involving club used as weapon
item.description: Scott Denning's swollen mugshot tells the story of a golf course brawl that left one man unconscious and another hit in the head with a golf club.
item.content:encoded:
A Kansas man spent the weekend in jail after he got into a nasty brawl with three other men on a golf course on Friday evening. His trip to the county jail came after a visit to a local hospital.

He might have been the one that ended up in handcuffs, but he wasn't the only one dishing out the damage. The entire side of his face ended up being a swollen mess in a picture taken by the jail.

Scott Denning, 52, of Winfield, Kansas was booked early Saturday morning into the Sedgwick County Jail for aggravated assault, aggravated battery, assault, battery, and criminal damage to property, reports Kake News.

According to the Wichita Police Department, officers responded to the Arthur B. Sim Golf Course around 6:20 pm on Friday for a disturbance. Denning and three Wichita men had been involved in a brawl.

The preliminary investigation found that Denning had approached the three men to apologize for an errant shot. An argument took place followed by a physical altercation.

As you can see, Denning was on the receiving end of some of that physical altercation. His face is unbelievably swollen. But he wasn’t the only one hurt in the exchange, according to police.

MAN TOOK A TRIP TO A MYRTLE BEACH GROCERY STORE, GETS BEATEN WITH METAL BAT CONFRONTING WIFE'S BOYFRIEND

A 38-year-old Wichita man was knocked unconscious at some point. Police say the other two Wichita men, 28 and 52, were chased with a golf club and one of them was hit in the head with it.

Does that mean the apology for the errant shot wasn't accepted? It certainly seems that's the case. Denning was treated at the hospital before being booked into jail on a $50,000 bond.

As of Tuesday afternoon, Denning remained in the Sedgwick County Jail. There were no other arrests and the investigation, reports Kake News, is ongoing.

item.title: Florida State fans pining for Jimbo Fisher's return are living in the past, not in reality
item.description: Congratulations Seminoles fans on ousting AD Michael Alford, but Jimbo Fisher's age and Texas A&M struggles make his FSU return a tough sell.
item.content:encoded:
Congratulations, Seminoles fans, part one of your master plan to return to the pantheon of college football has been completed.

For those unaware, Florida State fired their embattled athletic director, Michael Alford, earlier this week.

The reason that's so significant is multifaceted, but his main transgression and the thing that ultimately lost him his job was the recent skid of the once-proud FSU football team.

And that all ties back to a decision Alford made back in 2024, when he gifted head coach Mike Norvell a massive contract extension with an almost absurd buyout.

The monetary numbers were questionable, even at a time when Norvell and the Noles were trending in the right direction, but since then, the program has taken a sharp downturn, punctuated by an 8-18 record since their ACC Championship winning season in 2023.

DID ALABAMA DOOM THEMSELVES TO MEDIOCRITY WITH KALEN DEBOER EXTENSION?

So, now that Alford is sunk, the man he chose to anchor himself to has to be on the way out as well, right?

In theory, yes, but there's still that pesky buyout number that keeps getting brought up.

And then there's the other question that gets raised whenever schools even think about firing their current head coach: who can we hire?

There are a ton of quality names out there that the Seminoles should absolutely consider as their next head coach, but one of the only names I keep seeing tossed around by fans on social media is former Florida State head coach Jimbo Fisher.

KEEP AN EYE ON THESE UNDER-THE-RADAR NAMES DURING THIS SEASON'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHING CAROUSEL

I get it.

Things are brutal right now in Tallahassee, and Noles fans are just trying to cling onto something from the good old days, but I'm not so sure if Fisher is the answer.

Let's start with his age.

Fisher turns 61 in October, and while plenty of great coaches have had phenomenal seasons well into their 60s and 70s, the former FSU and Texas A&M head man hasn't donned a headset in three years, which might as well be dog years given how different the game of college football looks now.

Speaking of Texas A&M, Fisher's last stop as a head coach with the Aggies left a lot to be desired.

While in College Station, Fisher compiled a 45-25 record, which is fine, but definitely not what he was hired to do.

His five and a half years as the Aggies' head coach was marred by inconsistent offenses and power struggles, as his inability to hand over the controls on offense before it was too late is partially what led to his demise.

One of the reasons Fisher left the confines of Tallahassee - where he had won a national championship - for Texas A&M was (allegedly) the fact that Florida State would not meet his demands for more resourcing.

The Aggies are one of the most well-resourced football programs in America, and the fact that he was never able to even make an SEC Championship Game shouldn't inspire confidence.

I doubt the Seminoles are in a position, financially speaking, to give Fisher the funds he needs to compete on the national stage, and even if they do, would he be able to wind back the clocks and have FSU looking like the mid 2010s version of themselves?

As I said earlier, I totally get it.

As a Gator fan, when things were coming to a merciful end with Billy Napier, I started to talk myself into the idea of Urban Meyer coming home and coaching Florida again.

But being realistic, that would have never worked.

Meyer flamed out at his final stop in Jacksonville and he was nearly a decade removed from coaching in college football.

Florida State needs to move forward, not backward.

Find a hot, up-and-coming coach that will thrust the Seminoles into the modern era of college football.

Just off the top of my head, a guy like Boise State's Spencer Danielson would be a home run hire to get the Noles back to where they want to be.

But, of course, Florida State needs to find a new AD first.

Then, after that, they have to actually fire Norvell, a prospect that might not be as simple as just pulling the plug given his exorbitant buyout.

There are a lot of problems in Tallahassee right now, but there are plenty of solutions as well.

I'm not so sure hiring Jimbo Fisher is one of them.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Inside Vance's intimate Capitol Hill huddle as Republicans confront tough midterm terrain
item.description: JD Vance urged Republican lawmakers on Capitol Hill to hammer crime, inflation and prescription drug costs on the campaign trail ahead of reelection.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Vice President JD Vance energized Republicans during a huddle on Capitol Hill Tuesday where he urged lawmakers to "kick a--" in the 49 days before the midterm elections, according to audio obtained by Fox News Digital from a person in the room.

He wants members of Congress who are on the campaign trail to tell Americans how Trump administration's policies benefit them daily.

"There's people out there right now whose lives are going to get better, or their lives are going to get worse based on whether we're in the majority or whether we're in the minority," Vance told the Republican lawmakers in spelling out the stakes of the 2026 midterms.

"There are going to be people who are going to be poorer. Who are going to be less able to afford their prescription drugs, who are going to be less safe in the homes in their neighborhoods if the other guys get the majority," he continued. "And there are people who are going to be able to walk down the street in safety if you guys keep the majority. If we keep the majority together."

Specifically, Vance told incumbents to hammer home the issue of crime, noting that the homicide rate has reached a 126-year low. Vance explained that in a country of 330 million people, that crime stat translates to "thousands of people," including mothers and fathers, who are coming home to their families instead of being victims of deadly crimes.

FBI REPORTS LARGEST DROP IN VIOLENT CRIME AND MURDER SINCE 1937 AS HOMICIDES FALL MORE THAN 18%

"There are tens of thousands of children who will come home tonight and work on their homework with mom or dad, rather than a stranger, because of what we've been able to do in supporting law enforcement," Vance said in the closed-door meeting.

"This is not an abstraction, ladies and gentlemen," the vice president continued. "This is not about what you see on CNN or Fox News. This is not whether someone with an 'R' or a 'D' next to their name wins. This is about whether the American people in this country that we love have a government that they deserve, that protects them, that fights for them, or whether they have a government that treats them as a means to end."

Fox News Digital caught up with some lawmakers after the meeting.

One House Republican granted anonymity to speak candidly told Fox News Digital the meeting was  "a pep rally for the midterms. It was about raising money, showing up, making sure that everybody's all hands on deck going into November."

"I think he did a great job," Rep. Tim Burchett, R- Tenn., assessed. "He's very good. He's very personable."

"He's got some kind of voodoo thing going on where he remembers everybody's dadgum name," Burchett told Fox News Digital. "It kind of freaks me out a little bit. But, I mean, every time I've run into him — I remember one time I was waiting in line to go to the bathroom and he walked out of the bathroom. 'Hey, Tim, what's going on?' I invited him to a [University of Tennessee] game."

Vance offered some campaign tips to the lawmakers while ribbing the political consulting class for sometimes being out of touch, and saying "the American people are not dumb."

He said voters understand President Donald Trump and his administration inherited problems, including inflation, massive debt and "a country that was weaker on the national stage."

"They know that Rome wasn't built in a day," he said.

THE ONE LINE FROM JD VANCE’S GOP KEYNOTE THAT REVEALS HIS VISION FOR AMERICA

The vice president directed members to "pound the pavement" in their home districts to personally connect with as many voters as possible.

Just as importantly, Vance said, Republicans in safe districts who have no real opposition from the left should contribute money to the campaigns of fellow Republicans who are in competitive districts.

"So here's the thing, this is not rocket science. You guys know this better than I do, you know your districts better than I do," Vance said . "We know that most voters, particularly the voters who are open-minded, who are not hardcore partisans, they don't really start paying attention to the election until right about now."

THUNE-ALIGNED GROUPS UNLEASH HISTORIC WAR CHEST TO DEFEND SENATE MAJORITY: 'WINNING MESSAGE'

Vance also spoke fondly of when late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina joined him in Ohio while he was campaigning for the Senate in 2022.

"I'll never forget this," said Vance. " Lindsey Graham comes out — I didn't know Lindsey Graham at all, and you guys know how the campaign trail is in the final stretches. You wake up in a crappy hotel, you haven't seen your wife, your kids in a few days, and it's a lot more fun when you have some company out there."

"You're telling jokes, you're enjoying it. That energy — people pick up on it. So, get out there and campaign with your friends."

Vance recalled how Graham told him stories that had him "aching with laughter," half of which he said he could not repeat.

One source told Fox News Digital that Vance stayed after his remarks in tacit encouragement for House Republicans to pledge more money to their campaign arm, which several did. One person said Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, for example, pledged $1.1 million to the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC).

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters afterward that the meeting raised $20 million toward Republicans' re-election efforts.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh shares major regret after Chargers stunning Week 1 loss to Cardinals
item.description: Jim Harbaugh said in retrospect that the Los Angeles Chargers' starters had more preseason reps after turnovers and sloppy play doomed their Week 1 loss.
item.content:encoded:
Jim Harbaugh had an eye-opening regret after the Los Angeles Chargers' stunning Week 1 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

After losing 26-14 to a Cardinals team that many expected to struggle mightily this season, the 62-year-old coach lamented the Chargers' preseason preparation.

"We made some preseason-type of mistakes," Harbaugh said during the team’s press conference on Monday. "Now in retrospect, I wish we’d played our guys a little bit more in the preseason and given them those reps."

The Chargers played their starters for brief stints in the team’s second and third preseason games, but clearly that wasn’t enough. Last season, the 3-14 Cardinals allowed 20.9 points per game, which was tied for 21st in the NFL with the Washington Commanders, but looked much better on Sunday.

Against a team that lost their last nine games last season, the Chargers' offense scored just two touchdowns in the loss. The offense sputtered after losing Ladd McConkey to an injury in the third quarter.

Prior to leaving the game, McConkey recorded five catches for 82 yards and a touchdown. Harbaugh said the star wide receiver is day to day with a rib injury.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Chargers trailed by just two points when the former Georgia star left the game, and they did not score after McConkey’s departure.

In the loss, the Chargers had a blocked punt, an interception and another drive that ended with a turnover on downs. After the game on Sunday, Harbaugh called the performance sloppy.

"Some uncharacteristic things happened. Give (the Cardinals) credit for making them happen," Harbaugh said on Sunday. "I would call it sloppy at times. Too sloppy. That’s something we need to get fixed."

The Chargers will look to fix their mistakes when the play the Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at home at 4:25 p.m. EST on Sunday.

item.title: Roman Reigns survives Penta's World Heavyweight Championship challenge, LA Knight makes a statement of his own

item.content:encoded:
Roman Reigns and Penta put on an instant classic in Mexico City and it was one of the best "Monday Night Raw" matches of the year.

Penta was challenging for the World Heavyweight Championship after winning a No. 1 contender tournament, defeating several Luchadores for a shot at Roman Reigns. Penta had all of Mexico in his corner from the jump. He came out wearing a headdress to put an exclamation point on his already riveting entrance. He knew it would take everything he had to take the belt off Reigns and that the "Tribal Chief" wasn’t going to make it easy for him.

Reigns let Penta come to him for the most part. He tried to slow down the match as much as he could. The match changed in Penta’s favor after performing The Sacrifice on Reigns’ right arm. Reigns was obstructed from doing his usual moves without feeling any pain. He persevered through it and kicked out of a Penta Driver and a Mexican Destroyer in the process.

Penta’s lone mistake was going for a high-risk move toward the end of the match. He was met with a Superman punch. Reigns flopped into the corner and waited for the right moment to strike with a spear. He connected and pinned Penta for the win.

The crowd in Mexico City was absolutely heartbroken as Reigns crushed the dreams of their hero. Penta went up the ramp in disbelief as "Monday Night Raw" went off the air.

item.title: Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz's 'effective altruism' network tied to AI regulation push
item.description: Billionaire Democratic megadonor Dustin Moskovitz-backed "effective altruism" funder Coefficient Giving eyes $1B artificial intelligence push amid doomerism concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Concerns about artificial intelligence spelling doom for the human race are being linked to a "cult-like" philanthropy movement known as "effective altruism" supported by billionaire Democratic megadonor and Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz, according to a policy analyst.

In response to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation announcement on X, Parker Thayer, an investigative researcher at Capital Research Center in Washington D.C., went viral as he raised questions about whether the resignation was part of a broader network that aims to influence lawmakers and AI policy.

"I resigned from Anthropic today," Coxon’s post read. "I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives."

RESEARCHER WHO DEPARTED AI ROLE OVER FEARS OF RACING INTO EXTINCTION SAYS PEOPLE ARE 'BEGGING' FOR REGULATION

Thayer quoted the post in a response that received interaction online with top lawmakers in Congress, including Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

"This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion," Thayer posted. "The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting."

Thayer echoed claims made by White House AI advisor David Sacks that AI fears are overblown and potentially based on political motives.

"I think this is becoming a panic," Sacks told CBS News correspondent Jo Ling Kent. "We're in an election season, and there is an incentive for political actors to try and amplify the fear. And I think this is a moment to really calm down a little bit and look at the issue rationally."

SEN. BERNIE SANDERS: YES, WE MUST HIT THE PAUSE BUTTON ON AI BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE

Coxon told Fox News’ Bret Baier last week that we are "on the doorstep of tremendous discoveries," but are running in too quickly. He emphasized the need for moderation.

Baier asked Coxon if the issue could be figured out.

"I think definitely. I think if we actually try instead of submitting to the inevitability of a doomed race or a hubristic gamble, then we can solve it," he said. "The problem is not unsolvable."

TOP MEDIA OUTLETS FAIL TO DISCLOSE WHO IS BANKROLLING THEIR AI REPORTERS

Coxon said he was acting alone when deciding to voice his concerns about the direction of AI, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Fox News Digital sat down with Thayer to ask about his theories concerning the coordination behind Coxon's "sophisticated" resignation, which was in turn met with a slew of national television interviews and immediate notoriety. Almost overnight, Coxon's post became a major point of policy debate spanning across political parties and politicians, including President Donald Trump and socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Thayer did not offer a theory for which individuals or groups might have coordinated with Coxon, who has denied such claims. But Thayer said the "AI doomerism movement" is associated with "effective altruism," a philosophy he described as "cult-like."

OPINION: REP. TED LIEU: AI IS ALREADY TOO POWERFUL. WE NEED A KILL SWITCH BEFORE DISASTER STRIKES

According to the Centre for Effective Altruism, the movement is defined as a "project that aims to find the best ways to help others and put them into practice."

But Thayer noted that while the philanthropic movement may sound high-minded, Silicon Valley elites and members who donate and support "effective altruism" may have much more direct political goals in mind.

Thayer did not have evidence that any individuals or groups connected to the effective altruism movement provided public relations or other support for Coxon’s post about his resignation.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Moskovitz and his wife Cari Tuna have been leading financial backers of organizations associated with the "effective altruism" movement.

The couple founded Coefficient Giving, formerly known as Open Philanthropy, and remain its "main funders," according to the organization. Tuna serves as its president.

Coefficient Giving says its artificial intelligence work has expanded rapidly, with $168 million committed to AI safety, security and field-building in 2024 and $351 million in 2025 — a combined $519 million. The organization says it is on track to commit more than $1 billion to AI policy advocacy in 2026.

In a 2021 grant application description, the organization cited that it seeks "to fund programs and events in a variety of areas of interest to Coefficient Giving — including effective altruism, global catastrophic risks, biosecurity, AI for epistemics, forecasting, and other areas."

Moskovitz, who Forbes estimates has a net worth of roughly $10 billion, contributed more than $50 million to support the Biden-Harris campaign from 2020 to 2024, including $46.89 million to the Future Forward PAC, which served as the main fundraising vessel for the failed presidential campaign.

TRUMP UNLOADS ON TECH TITANS PUSHING FOR SLOWDOWN ON EMERGING INDUSTRY: ‘WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!’

On Monday, the Department of War Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering posted to X: "Americanism, not effective altruism. The United States will continue to be AI DOMINANT!"

As for the reasoning behind "effective altruism’s" commitment to the artificial intelligence policy space, Thayer said the fearmongering technique is comparable to the climate change narrative that has been traditionally peddled by the Democratic Party.

"They basically just say kind of in the same vein as climate change activists like Al Gore used to, they kind of just make bombastic doomsday projections without citing really a whole lot of easily discernible evidence and just expect us to trust their expertise," Thayer explained.

"First, they got you scared of the data centers based on a bunch of sketchy arguments about water pollution supposedly, and supposedly raising your electric prices, which don't seem to actually be true," he added. "And now they're getting you scared of the actual AI that the data centers are being used to launch."

Thayer said that if AI critics were truly afraid of a potential doomsday scenario, they would be advocating for the extinction of artificial intelligence altogether. Instead, he says that it is a tactic to increase the government’s power over the industry while also acting in their own interest so "that they're the only ones who are allowed to build it."

In an opinion piece published in Medium in 2024, Moskovitz noted that he was concerned about the potential risks AI poses, saying that a potential doomsday "situation may develop extremely quickly."

"Contrary to the popular narrative about effective altruists working in AI, my interest in mitigating the potential risks isn’t rooted in specific predictions about the far future, but rather simple concern about the next few decades, when I and the people I care about are still alive to care about what happens," he wrote.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-LA, said a meeting at the White House to discuss AI policy could happen before the end of this week or the next. Trump also weighed in on the AI outlook in a post to Truth Social on Monday.

"The people that say AI is going to destroy the World, and that Data Centers are bad for your neighborhood, are the same people that said, just a short time ago, that the World would be extinguished by "Climate Change." That HOAX never worked out for them, and now they’re on to the next one."

Fox News Digital reached out to Moskovitz, Coefficient Giving and Coxon for comment.

item.title: Kamala Harris viciously mocked with resurfaced bumbling 'two words' explanation of AI after desperate call
item.description: Kamala Harris' rambling 2023 explanation of AI as "two letters" resurfaces after she posted a lengthy call to slow down AI development online.
item.content:encoded:
Former Vice President and failed presidential candidate Kamala Harris is being mocked over a resurfaced clip of her "two letters" explanation of artificial intelligence after she posted a call to slow its development.

Harris, who previously served as the Biden administration's AI czar, posted a lengthy statement on AI on Monday. In her post, Harris called for President Donald Trump to "do his job to protect America’s interests by pursuing a treaty with countries like China to stop dangerous uses of AI, limit the speed of its development, and adopt global standards for testing."

In response, social media users recalled Harris’ attempt at explaining AI as vice president in 2023.

"I think the first part of this issue that should be articulated is AI is kind of a fancy thing," Harris said. "First of all, it's two letters. It means artificial intelligence, but ultimately what it is is it's about machine learning."

WATCH: KAMALA HARRIS TORCHED OVER ‘ZERO SENSE’ WNBA PEP TALK IN LATEST ‘WORD SALAD’ MOMENT

She continued, saying, "And so, the machine is taught — and part of the issue here is what information is going into the machine that will then determine — and we can predict then, if we think about what information is going in, what then will be produced in terms of decisions and opinions that may be made through that process."

"So," she went on even further, "to reduce it down to its most simple point, this is part of the issue that we have here is thinking about what is going into a decision, and then whether that decision is actually legitimate and reflective of the needs and the life experiences of all the people."

After Harris' X post on Monday, conservative influencer "Western Lensman" reposted the 2023 video of Harris, writing, "Kamala Harris on AI when it's not a written statement crafted by a team of consultants."

National security and global economics expert Kyle Bass reacted, "There’s not a chance in hell Kamala wrote this. Have you ever heard her say ‘frontier,’ ‘advancing,’ and ‘intelligence’ in the same sentence? Until now, her misfits had never produced anything this un-Kamala and then posted it on social media."

Columnist S.L. Kanthan wrote, "One of the dumbest women now wants America to voluntarily slow down progress in AI." He posted another video of Harris explaining cloud storage.

Harris said, "No longer are you necessarily keeping those private files in some file cabinet that’s locked in the basement of the house. It’s on your laptop, and it's then, therefore, up here in this cloud, that exists above us, right?"

Author and national security expert Sarah Adams commented on Harris’ AI post, writing, "No one is looking for your thoughts on 'intelligence.'"

Another user, influencer Andrew Aziz, and several others suggested that Harris’ post itself was AI-generated.

KAMALA HARRIS DIVES INTO MIDTERM FIGHT ONLY TO GET ROASTED FOR NEVER HAVING 'AN ORIGINAL THOUGHT IN HER LIFE’

In her post, Harris wrote that AI is "advancing at an alarming speed," emphasizing what she characterized as industry leaders’ call to "responsibly slow the pace of frontier AI development."

She wrote that "a slowdown is critical in order to ensure AI serves the public interest," saying, "Pacing AI development does not mean giving up on this technology’s potential to produce life-saving benefits in fields like medicine — some of which we are already seeing. Rather, it is about setting up sensible guardrails so that AI does not completely escape human control and endanger our safety and collective future."

Besides action from Trump, Harris called on Congress to "work at an urgent pace" to provide AI oversight, saying, "The United States must continue to lead the world in developing AI technology even as we seek to impose common-sense safety standards."

Harris is not the only prominent Democrat to have called for increased AI regulation recently. Former President Barack Obama urged Democrats during a private fundraiser in New York City on Thursday to place artificial intelligence near the center of their political agenda ahead of the midterms and the 2028 presidential race while warning that the technology could become dangerous without greater oversight as voters increasingly raise concerns about jobs, privacy and data centers.

"This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous," Obama said. "If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases. I do think that this can help us figure out pathways for a clean energy future."

ANTHROPIC CEO CALLS ON AI INDUSTRY TO SLOW DOWN TECH RACE, DRAWING SUPPORT FROM ELON MUSK, SAM ALTMAN

Meanwhile, Trump on Monday rejected growing calls for safeguards and restrictions on AI, declaring that the technology needs a "STRONG AND SMART" president rather than additional restraints.

"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

He suggested that "there is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China," adding, "WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so."

Fox News Digital's Lindsay Kornick and Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

item.title: Joe Manchin calls on Trump to freeze AI IPOs, claims president has 'power to save humanity'
item.description: Joe Manchin urged Trump to freeze AI IPOs until Congress passes safeguards, but critics say blocking capital markets won't address the real risks.
item.content:encoded:
Former Sen. Joe Machin, D-W.Va., called on President Donald Trump during a Monday appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" to use executive authority to pause new artificial intelligence IPOs until Congress passes legislation establishing safeguards for the rapidly developing technology.

Manchin framed the request as an urgent step to prevent companies developing advanced AI from facing additional pressure to race ahead before lawmakers establish rules governing the technology.

"The president of the United States has the power to save humanity," Manchin said. "They must be concerned about this thing can take off and think on its own and make its own decisions and override anything of humans and we can't stop it. If that's what they're concerned about, then stop it now when you can."

LIZ PEEK: AI ALARM BELLS ARE RINGING AND TRUMP NEEDS TO TAKE THEM SERIOUSLY

Republican National Committee member and Human First chairwoman Amy Kremer, who had previously called for AI safeguards while opposing a broad moratorium, pushed back on Machin's specific proposal, saying an IPO freeze would interfere with capital markets without addressing the underlying safety concerns.

"I do not support a president using executive authority to interfere with the markets," Kremer said in a Tuesday statement to Fox News Digital. "An IPO freeze is the kind of top-down mandate that conservatives have long opposed, and it would not even address the actual risk."

"What the president should use his executive power for is to demand pre-deployment testing begin immediately. That is where the real safeguards belong, not in blocking companies from raising capital," she continued.

PRESIDENTIAL FLIP? GOP INSIDER PREDICTS TRUMP CHANGE OF MIND ON KEY AI POLICY AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

The White House, in a statement to Fox News Digital, pointed to three Truth Social posts from Trump addressing the growing debate over AI risks and efforts to slow the technology's development.

Trump separately rejected growing calls Monday for additional AI restrictions, arguing the United States should not give up its lead over China and saying existing government powers could be used against companies engaged in wrongdoing.

Trump said additional regulatory "guardrails" were not the answer to concerns surrounding the technology.

"The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump said.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

The debate intensified after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for frontier AI developers to slow the pace at which they increase the capabilities for their most powerful models.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk were among the technology leaders who expressed support for slowing frontier development, while Trump and other Republicans warned that unilateral U.S. restrictions could benefit China.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., rejected an emergency AI moratorium on Sunday, telling CNN that Congress should work with AI companies to determine appropriate safeguards rather than abruptly halt development.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Kremer told Fox News Digital that the escalating dispute also reflected what she views as Congress’ failure to establish clear federal AI rules before the technology reached its current stage.

"This moment is a reminder of what happens when Republicans do not govern," she said. "When Republicans fail to act, the solutions Democrats offer will be disastrous. Lawmakers have had years to establish clear rules for artificial intelligence, and they have not done it. The responsibility now falls on the executive branch to act where Congress will not."

The Trump administration has already established a voluntary federal framework for evaluating advanced AI models. 

Trump's June executive order allows developers of covered frontier models to give the federal government secure early access before release for testing and cybersecurity purposes, while explicitly stating that the framework does not create mandatory federal licensing, pre-clearance or permitting requirements.

item.title: ‘Still waiting on the DOGE check’: Battleground state voters cast doubt on Trump’s new $5K promise
item.description: Detroit, Michigan, residents call gas prices, car insurance and rent "ridiculous" while dismissing Trump's $5,000 dividend as political "bribery."
item.content:encoded:
Voters squeezed by rising costs are skeptical of President Donald Trump’s proposed $5,000 dividend — with at least one resident pointing to a previous DOGE dividend proposal that never materialized.

"I feel like that's a pitch to get more votes," Yolanda Lewis told Fox News Digital. "I'm still waiting on the DOGE check that he promised that we never received, so until he gives us a definite date saying when we're gonna get that and receive it, then I'll take that into consideration."

Trump suggested in February 2025 that a portion of savings generated by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) could be returned to taxpayers, while Elon Musk entertained a proposal that envisioned payments of as much as $5,000. Trump later backed the idea of returning 20% of DOGE savings to Americans. DOGE reported $110.3 billion in savings from contracts, grants and leases, though a Government Accountability Office review later found that some of its estimates were inaccurate or lacked sufficient supporting evidence.

Now, with affordability a top-of-mind issue for voters across the country, Trump has unveiled a new "Trump dividend" plan at the Midterm GOP Convention last Wednesday that would give $5,000 to American adults if Republicans maintain control of Congress.

Several Detroit voters, interviewed by Fox News Digital at the Detroit Health Department’s annual Block Party on Sept. 12, rejected the proposal, with some calling it a "bribe" and others questioning whether the money would ever be paid out.

TRUMP MAKES STUNNING FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND CASH PROMISE IN BID TO RALLY GOP VOTERS AT DALLAS MIDTERM CONVENTION

"I think it's kind of irresponsible because what is the long-term impact of this money?" Jahdante Smith, the Green Party candidate for the state House of Representatives 9th district, told Fox News Digital.

Smith, who supports Medicare for All, pointed to the nation's roughly $40 trillion debt in questioning how the proposal would be funded.

"So where does that money come from? Where do you divert those funds from? Also, I think that it is sort of a bribe," Smith said.

Michigan, which Trump won by 1.4% in 2024, has become a key battleground in the fight for Senate control as Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Saye and Republican Mike Rogers are both vying for Michigan's open Senate seat.

El-Sayed called Trump's $5,000 proposal "unserious" during a rally in Lansing, Michigan.

"Funny thing about it is like there's no world in which you can pay for it," El-Sayed said. "So how about you actually do some governing and like solve the Social Security problem. How about we guarantee people health care so they don't have to pay so much for that."

Rogers' campaign did not directly comment on the former congressman's stance on Trump's $5,000 dividend plan. Instead, it pointed to El-Sayed's support for implementing a progressive tax plan.

"You know what’s not serious? Challenging Mike to a 1:1 football scrimmage, taking money from Designated Terrorist Organizations and advocating to raise taxes for Michiganders while they’re already paying for Democrats’ mismanagement," said Alyssa Brouillet, communications director for the Rogers campaign. "Funny enough, those are things Abdul does."

Prices are an acute concern in Detroit, where roughly a third of residents live below the federal poverty line. The city's median household income is below $40,000, according to U.S. census data.

"Well, as a city Detroit retiree, affordability is very important, and I think the prices since Trump's been back in office have gone up on everything, especially gas, diesel, you know, affordabilities went out the window," William Davis told Fox News Digital.

The current cost of gas in Detroit is $4.11 per gallon. Before the Iran war, gas prices hovered between $2.81 and $2.92 per gallon in January.

TRUMP FACES RECKONING AS GOP FIGURES LABEL $5K PROMISE A 'SOCIALIST VOTE-BUYING SCHEME'

Martesha Adams, a young mother and nurse living in Detroit, told Fox News Digital at the Detroit Health Department Block Party that she also viewed the $5,000 proposal as an attempt to win over struggling Americans.

"The whole time I feel that he's been in the office, it's been a kind of game," Adams said. "America has been laughed at from everywhere. And the $5K for bribery, that's nothing. So I hope that people do not go for that bribe, and they really look into the politics."

For Shelby Campbell, a 2023 graduate of Wayne State University, affordability has already forced significant changes. She said she sold her car because she could no longer afford Michigan's no-fault auto insurance and has struggled to find an affordable rental in Detroit.

Campbell called Trump's $5,000 proposal "disgusting."

"He shouldn't be able to offer people money if we have one party in office," Campbell said. "It's supposed to be about everybody and what we all want and need, so it's just bribery in my opinion."

Campbell, who said she plans to vote for El-Sayed in the general election, argued that money already plays too large a role in politics.

"I think he's genuinely a good guy, and he wants to get money out of politics, and I am all for that," Campbell said. "We seriously need that because big corporations buy our elections just like Donald Trump is trying to do."

Other Detroit residents echoed Lewis' skepticism about whether Trump would actually deliver the proposed payments.

BILLIONS SPENT BY KEY FEDERAL AGENCY HASN'T MADE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP ANY EASIER: REPORT

Trump also proposed a separate $2,000 dividend last year funded by tariff revenue, though those payments never materialized.

"I don't think it's realistic to think he's going to do that," Davis said of Trump's latest proposal.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said Sunday on "Meet the Press" that the $5,000 payments would require congressional approval, while pledging to work toward Trump's proposal.

"I never go out and give big commitments on the front end because I’ve got to work through it, and that’s what we do every single day," Johnson said.

While Trump's proposal has garnered mixed reactions within the Republican Party, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, posted on X that he'd work to prepare a bill and get it passed before the election.

House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., rejected the idea that Trump was seeking to "bribe" voters.

"The only thing that I knew of was that he has this concept of a dividend of all Americans being able to share in the success of America," Emmer told Politico.

"Let the policy guys draft it. Let them debate it. Let them move it through committee," Emmer told Politico. "You get it to the whip’s office. We’ll pass it."
